turns.en: There's a podcast called Song Exploder, I believe, that is a similar concept that's not in Hebrew, in English, that I'll point people to if you love that one.
turns.zh: 有个叫《歌曲解析器》的播客，理念类似，但不是希伯来语的，是英文的，如果你们喜欢那个播客，我可以推荐给你们。

turns.speaker: Tomer Cohen
turns.en: That's awesome.
turns.zh: 太棒了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Is there a product you've recently discovered that you really love? Could be an app, could be some clothing, could be a kitchen gadget, type gadget.
turns.zh: 最近有没有你发现的特别喜欢的产品？可以是app、衣服、厨房小工具之类的。

turns.speaker: Tomer Cohen
turns.en: Can it can be a product I want to have, which I think is actually really easy to do?
turns.zh: 可以是让我想拥有的产品，我觉得这其实挺容易做到的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I love that. This is a product thinking 101 and just the vision of what you want to see.
turns.zh: 我喜欢这个。这就是产品思维的入门阶段，构想你想看到的东西。

turns.speaker: Tomer Cohen
turns.en: So in my car right now, there's Alexa built-in, which is great because the kids can ask for songs all day long and it's a whole show inside of the car. But one of my favorite things to do when this has been doing it for well over two years is I go in and I go into voice mode.
turns.zh: 我现在车里装了Alexa，特别棒，因为孩子们整天都能用它点歌，车里就像个小型演唱会。但用了两年多最让我喜欢的功能是进入语音模式。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: ChatGPT.
turns.zh: ChatGPT。

turns.speaker: Tomer Cohen
turns.en: Yeah, ChatGPT, and then just have a conversation, and that's just friction. I would love to have on my steering wheel a button that invokes my AI friend that can sit next to me in the passenger seat, and I just think that would be such a... I actually think it would [inaudible 01:01:36] rides for people. Just that movement, that's just like elimination of friction will transform the experience for me.
turns.zh: 是啊，ChatGPT，然后就是和它对话，这就是摩擦。我希望在我的方向盘上能有一个按钮，召唤我的AI朋友，让它坐在副驾驶座上。我觉得这会非常……实际上我认为这会（音频中断）给人们带来更好的体验。只要消除这种摩擦，整个体验就会焕然一新。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: On that note, I recently discovered Teslas actually do this now. If you hold the right wheel, Grok appears and you could talk to Grok. So it's here. The AI has arrived. Yeah. I just did it by accident and then it's, "Okay, cool."
turns.zh: 说到这，我最近发现特斯拉已经实现了这一点。只要按住右侧的方向盘，Grok就会出现，你可以和它对话。所以这项功能已经上线了。AI 时代真的来了。是啊，我刚刚不小心试了一下，然后它就回应：“好的，太棒了。”

turns.speaker: Tomer Cohen
turns.en: Great. So for me, if anybody from Rivian is listening, please bring this in the car.
turns.zh: 太好了。所以对我们来说，如果Rivian的团队在听的话，请把这项功能加到车里。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Rivian's falling behind. Yeah. And you have to use Grok. It'd be cool if you could switch to different AIs because it has a personality. Just give me information. I don't need you to laugh and give me jokes.
turns.zh: Rivian已经落后了。是啊。你得用Grok。如果能切换到不同的AI就更好了，因为它们都有各自的个性。只要给我信息就行，我不需要它讲笑话。

turns.speaker: Tomer Cohen
turns.en: Did you need to spend some time with it before or did it have any memory from... Did you bring any memory into it?
turns.zh: 你之前需要花时间训练它吗？还是它有记忆功能？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: There's a logged out version and then you could just log in and it connects to your account. Yeah, it's extremely cool. No one's talking about it. It's crazy because I don't know if they launched it fully, but it just appeared.
turns.zh: 有登录版和未登录版之分，你登录后就能连接到你的账户。是啊，这功能太酷了。没人谈论它。这太疯狂了，因为我不知道他们是否已经全面推出，但它就突然出现了。

turns.speaker: Tomer Cohen
turns.en: Do you talk in the car a lot to it?
turns.zh: 你在车里经常和它对话吗？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I don't use it that much, to be honest, but I should. My wife just doesn't love Grok. I think the brand of Grok is a specific brand. And so she's like, "Don't talk to Grok in here with me."
turns.zh: 说实话，我用得不多，但我应该多用。我的妻子就是不喜欢Grok。我觉得Grok这个品牌有特定的定位。她会说：“别在车里和我说话。”

turns.speaker: Tomer Cohen
turns.en: I love voice mode, so I use it all the time.
turns.zh: 我喜欢语音模式，所以一直用它。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Yeah, I love voice mode too. It just interrupts too often. That's the issue there, right? It's just it stops.
turns.zh: 是啊，我也喜欢语音模式。但它太容易被打断了。这就是问题所在，对吧？它会突然停止。

turns.speaker: Tomer Cohen
turns.en: By the way, you can set it up. You can basically say like, "Hey, just let me finish."
turns.zh: 顺便说一句，你可以设置它。比如说：“嘿，让我先说完。”

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I now know that. I'm learning so much. Okay. Two more questions. Do you have a life motto that you often find useful in work or in life?
turns.zh: 现在我知道了。我学到了很多。好的，再问两个问题。你有没有一条人生格言，在工作或生活中经常用到？

turns.speaker: Tomer Cohen
turns.en: I think last time I talked about it, I most associated here with, I might be wrong, but I'm not confused, although I don't say it as much anymore. But I think the one I love, growth mindset is a second religions for us at home. And one thing I love about, there's a phrase there that is becoming is better than being, which I think ties into the FSB mode a little bit, which is you're always in progress mode, iteration mode. It's not about reaching a state. It's about the journey, the process. That's what you should fall in love with. It's about continuously growing and evolving without the negativity of it or there's no sense of FOMO there. It's just this continuous thing. If I look back a year from now and I look back, how much did I grow? How much do I know? What skills to do that again? Where are I becoming better? Do I feel like Tomer version 2026 versus 2025? What's the delta there? And I kind of love that as a way of thinking.
turns.zh: 我想上次我谈到过，我最常联系到的是……我可能记错了，但我没搞混，虽然我现在不常说了。但我最喜欢的是成长型思维模式，对我们家来说就像第二种宗教。其中有句话叫“成为比拥有更重要”，我觉得这和FSB模式有点关联，FSB模式就是你永远处于进步模式、迭代模式。重点不在于达到某种状态，而在于整个过程和旅程。这才是你应该热爱的。就是不断成长和进化，没有负面情绪，也没有错失恐惧。这就是持续的事情。一年后回头看，我成长了多少？我掌握了多少知识？要怎么再做一次？我在哪些方面变得更好了？2026年的我和2025年的我有什么不同？差距在哪里？我真的很喜欢这种思维方式。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: A great segue to our final question. By the time this episode comes out, it won't be a secret that you're leaving LinkedIn after 14 years. Legendary run. You joined way before the acquisition, you helped them integrate. Just like the way LinkedIn was perceived 14 years ago is so radically different from the way it is today. It's actually really fun and interesting to be there versus how people for a long time felt about LinkedIn. So I guess the question just how you feeling and what's next? I imagine you're going to get a lot of calls from a lot of people, but what are you planning?
turns.zh: 完美过渡到我们最后一个问题。等这期节目播出后，你离开领英14年的消息想必已不是秘密了。这是一段传奇般的历程。你远在领英被收购前就加入了公司，助力其整合业务。如今的领英与14年前相比简直天差地别。能身处其中与人们长期以来的看法形成鲜明对比，实在有趣又令人兴奋。所以我想问问你现在的心情如何，接下来有什么计划？我猜你会接到很多人的电话，但你有什么具体打算吗？

turns.speaker: Tomer Cohen
turns.en: Yeah, so I feel proud. It's been an incredible ride at LinkedIn. The way I've got to know about LinkedIn deeply the very first time was when I moved to the Valley and I went to a lecture at Stanford about social networks in 2008 and Reid was there and he talked about the power of being a professional communities online, and I was very nerdy about it and thought it was incredible vision, had no plans to join and actually started my own company after. But as luck would have it, found myself joining a few years after and just thought the mission was incredible. So in many ways it aligned with my purpose and just was an incredible ride to be here. (01:05:32): And I also feel very grateful. I shared this with the company recently. I was starting to take learnings from my experiences here. A lot of it was from tough situations. We had a lot of tough situations at LinkedIn and hard calls and late nights, but you learn so much from those and I'm just incredibly grateful. And I'm excited. I'm excited. I have a bias for change. I have a bias for kind of positioning myself in a place where I can learn the most and learn a lot. And it's an incredible time to build, so I'm just excited to be thinking of new problem sets and new areas where I can go deep on and invest the next decade in.
turns.zh: 是的，我深感自豪。在领英的这段旅程堪称非凡。我第一次深入了解领英，是2008年搬到硅谷后，去斯坦福大学听了一场关于社交网络的讲座。里德（Reid）在场，谈论了在线专业社区的力量。我当时对此非常着迷，觉得这是一个不可思议的愿景，虽然没打算加入，但后来创办了自己的公司。机缘巧合下，几年后我加入了领英，发现这里的使命与我的初衷高度契合。这段旅程堪称奇迹。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I think it's going to take a long time for you to not feel like you're working on LinkedIn and to forget about all the things that you have been worrying about for so many years.
turns.zh: 我深感感激。最近我和公司分享了这些感悟，从这段经历中汲取了许多教训。很多来自艰难时刻——领英经历过诸多挑战、深夜加班，但从中收获良多。我无比感恩，也满怀期待。未来十年，我将致力于探索新问题、开拓新领域，持续深耕。

turns.speaker: Tomer Cohen
turns.en: After you build something for such a long time, and I think you and I talked about it at one point, that I think one of the best traits for a builder is to become very passionate with what they're building. Really care. Not about the job. It's really care about the product. When you feel the pain when somebody complains and you kind of have this continuous discontent, and it's like for me, it's the notion of raising a baby. So yeah, it's hard. It will be hard. I will always think of LinkedIn as one of the babies I helped grow.
turns.zh: 当你为某件事奋斗多年，又深切关怀多年后再离开，确实会心有不舍。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Well, I'm excited to have you back someday when you figure out what you want to do next and or start whatever you're doing. I love that this was an excuse to get to know you. Tomer, thank you so much for being here.
turns.zh: 嗯，期待你未来某天回归，或是开启新征程。我很开心能借此机会深入了解你，托默（Tomer），感谢你的到来。

turns.speaker: Tomer Cohen
turns.en: It was great to be here. Thanks, Lenny.
turns.zh: 很荣幸能参与这场对话。谢谢你，莱尼（Lenny）。
